title: SublevelPLBoundedVariance.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable, bounded-below function with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. Convexity is not required; nonconvex objectives are permitted.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Sublevel α-gradient dominance: f(x)−inf f ≤ τ‖∇f(x)‖^α whenever f(x)≤f(x0), with 1≤α<2 and τ>0. The initial gap is at most Δ≥0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns g(x,ξ) using fresh iid randomness, with E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). Only gradient samples are returned; function values and shared-sample evaluations across different points are not supplied. E, L, τ, α, σ, Δ, ε, and x0 are public; f, g, the sampling law, and Ω are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SublevelPLBoundedVariance.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform second-moment noise bound E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ² for every x, with σ≥0. No stronger tail or samplewise smoothness condition is imposed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SublevelPLBoundedVariance.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible variance integrability and variance inequalities.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure; no dimension bound is specified.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SublevelPLBoundedVariance.lean: Public.normedE, Public.innerE, Public.finiteE, Public.measurableE, and Public.borelE.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Return an E-valued point X whose objective gap f(X)−inf_y f(y) is integrable and at most ε in expectation, with ε>0. No distance or gradient-norm requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[f(X)−inf f]≤ε over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, under the supplied fixed cap on total stochastic-gradient calls.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The combination of global smoothness, α-gradient dominance restricted to the initial sublevel set for α<2, gradient-only bounded-variance access, and unconditional expected objective accuracy is a meaningful localized variant requiring control of excursions outside that sublevel set.

descriptionHtml:
Sublevel Gradient Domination with Stochastic Gradients

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex differentiable function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, with L>0, and f⋆=infx∈Ef(x) is finite. Given x0∈E, assume f(x)−f⋆≤τ∥∇f(x)∥α whenever f(x)≤f(x0), where τ>0 and 1≤α<2. The oracle returns an unbiased stochastic gradient with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, using independent, identically distributed samples. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E with integrable objective gap and EP[f(x¯)−f⋆]≤ε, where P is the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, L, τ, α, σ, an initial-gap bound Δ≥0, the tolerance ε, and the given point x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 2 (Sublevel gradient domination). The function f is bounded below, and its initial sublevel set satisfies f(x)−f⋆≤τ∥∇f(x)∥αwhenever f(x)≤f(x0),f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Unbiased gradients with bounded variance). Let Ω be a measurable sample space and ν a probability measure on Ω. There is a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E such that, for every fixed x∈E, g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,⋅)−∇f(x)∥2 is integrable under ν, with Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),Eξ∼ν[∥g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)∥2]≤σ2. The samples (ξk)k≥0 have a joint probability law Q on ΩN. Each coordinate is measurable, the coordinates are mutually independent, and each has distribution ν. At query xk∈E, the oracle returns g(xk,ξk). The algorithm’s randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must have an integrable objective gap under P and satisfy EP[f(x¯)−f⋆]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f is differentiable, globally L-smooth and bounded below. With f⋆=infxf(x), assume f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ and f(x)−f⋆≤τ∥∇f(x)∥α whenever f(x)≤f(x0), where L,τ>0, 1≤α<2, σ,Δ≥0 and ε>0. The jointly measurable oracle uses IID samples from a probability measure p, with ∫g(x,z)dp(z)=∇f(x) and ∫∥g(x,z)−∇f(x)∥2dp(z)≤σ2; these integrals are integrable. The target is the unconditional last-iterate guarantee ∫[f(xK(ω))−f⋆]dP(ω)≤ε.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.SublevelPLBoundedVariance

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  L : ℝ
  τ : ℝ
  α : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.finiteE Public.measurableE Public.borelE

structure Params extends Public where
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.τ ∧ 1 ≤ p.α ∧ p.α < 2 ∧ 0 ≤ p.σ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    ∃ (g : p.E → p.Ω → p.E) (P0 : ProbabilityMeasure p.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → p.Ω)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → p.Ω) => ξ k)
      (P0 : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => p.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    BddBelow (Set.range f) ∧
    (∀ x, f x ≤ f p.x0 → f x - (⨅ y, f y) ≤ p.τ * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ p.α) ∧
    f p.x0 - (⨅ y, f y) ≤ p.Δ ∧
    Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (g x) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂(P0 : Measure _) = gradient f x) ∧
    (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2) (P0 : Measure _)) ∧
    (∀ x, ∫ ω, ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ∂(P0 : Measure _) ≤ p.σ ^ 2)
  successful p f output P :=
    Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - ⨅ y, f y) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, f (output ω) - ⨅ y, f y ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SublevelPLBoundedVariance
